title: Offline sync queue
prompt:
Implement the offline sync queue in queue.py.

This queue backs the mobile client's offline cache. Mutations made while offline
are queued and replayed in order once connectivity returns.

SyncQueue() must provide:
- push(kind, payload=None) -> the new mutation's id (a string, unique in this queue)
- pending() -> list of dicts {id, kind, payload}, oldest first. Must be a copy:
  mutating the returned list or its dicts must not affect the queue.
- ack(mutation_id) -> remove that mutation; True if it existed, else False.
- retry(mutation_id) -> move that mutation to the end of the queue; True if it
  existed, else False.
- __len__() -> number queued.
- to_dict() -> JSON-serialisable plain data.

Also provide from_dict(data) which rebuilds an equal queue. After a
round-trip through JSON the queue must contain the same pending() mutations in
the same order, and ids handed out later must never collide with restored ones.
IDs must also stay unique after ack/retry churn.

Only queue.py should change.
